physicalNotes: Radius 0.14452697 Jupiter radii from Giacalone et al. 2022 (2022AJ....163...99G), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163...99G/abstract): 10,332.5 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the mass 0.0102 Jupiter masses (the NASA Exoplanet Archive's calculated value (M-R relationship, its Chen & Kipping 2017 mass-radius relationship): a model, not a measurement, via the NASA Exoplanet Archive, https://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/docs/pscp_calc.html) times JPL's Jupiter GM. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: ExoFOP, via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname EXOFOP): P 0.3524597 d
sources.shape: Giacalone et al. 2022 (2022AJ....163...99G), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname GIACALONE_ET_AL__2022): a/R* derived from its semi-major axis 0.0097 au and stellar radius 0.94 solar radii; Giacalone et al. 2022 (2022AJ....163...99G), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname GIACALONE_ET_AL__2022): inclination derived from its impact parameter 0.77 with its a/R* 2.2189 (Winn 2010, eq. 7)
sources.eccentricity: No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular
sources.phase: ExoFOP, via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname EXOFOP): transit mid-time 2460423.375669 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 3 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
